# OMB M-26-04 — Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles

> **Federal policy, not NASA governance: binding on agencies as federal policy, a separate
> question from what NASA's own directives require.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary.
> It never by itself establishes what a specific NASA directive requires, and must not be
> cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President; signed by OMB Director Russell T. Vought |
| **Kind** | Policy memo (OMB Memorandum) |
| **Status** | Dated and effective December 11, 2025 [p.1]. Implements a July 23, 2025 Executive Order on "Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government" [p.1] — the document text itself is internally inconsistent on that order's number, giving "Executive Order 14139" in a footnote [p.1, n.1] and "Executive Order 14319" in the body text [p.1 and p.3, n.6]; the number is cited here as reported in the source, not resolved. Currently in force; by its own terms "sunsets two years after issuance unless OMB renews it" (paraphrase, p.3). |
| **Where to get it** | whitehouse.gov (OMB memoranda), free public. Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/M-26-04-Increasing-Public-Trust-in-Artificial-Intelligence-Through-Unbiased-AI-Principles-1.pdf` |
| **Binds whom** | "MEMORANDUM TO HEADS OF EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES" [p.1]; applies to any Large Language Model (LLM) procured by an agency, excludes National Security Systems (application there "encouraged" but not required) (paraphrase, p.2-3) |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** (our reading) This is the one document in the set targeting LLM ideological bias and truthfulness specifically, as a procurement/transparency requirement, rather than the general AI risk-management framework (M-25-21) or the acquisition-process mechanics (M-25-22) it cross-references. It is useful for seeing what the federal government requires of agency LLM procurement; it says nothing about what any specific NASA directive requires.

**Key content for artificial intelligence / machine-learning assurance.**
- [p.1] Overview: names the two "Unbiased AI Principles" from the Executive Order — Truth-seeking ("LLMs shall be truthful in responding to user prompts seeking factual information or analysis... and shall acknowledge uncertainty where reliable information is incomplete or contradictory") and Ideological Neutrality ("LLMs shall be neutral, nonpartisan tools that do not manipulate responses in favor of ideological dogmas") [p.1].
- [p.5] Appendix A, Sec. A: "A. Minimum Threshold for LLM Transparency. In solicitations for LLMs, agencies must request the following from a vendor: Acceptable Use Policy..." — a minimum-practice requirement, but one aimed at vendor transparency disclosures rather than a risk-management-practice regime of the kind M-25-21 defines.
- (paraphrase, p.3) new LLM solicitations must include contractual compliance requirements with the Unbiased AI Principles, existing contracts should be modified where practicable, and agency procurement policy must be updated by March 11, 2026, including a process for users to report outputs that violate the principles.
- No Chief AI Officer role and no "high-impact AI" determination appear anywhere in this memo (grep-checked); it defers entirely to M-25-21 for that framework and instead creates its own LLM-specific transparency minimums.
- AI touchpoints found by keyword grep: dense throughout, as expected for an LLM-focused memo — "AI," "LLM," and "artificial intelligence" appear in nearly every section; "automat..." and "algorithm" do not appear as defined terms; "machine learning" and "neural" are not used (the memo stays at the LLM/generative-AI level of description).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No direct counterpart on the current NASA document list; federal agency policy and NASA's own internal directives are kept as separate coverage axes in this project (our reading) — the nearest topical neighbor would be NASA-HDBK-2203 (the one document on the list that discusses AI/machine-learning assurance broadly), but it answers a different question (NASA's software engineering guidance for AI/ML components vs. federal procurement rules for LLM bias and truthfulness).
